message.reasoning: I'm thinking I should write a unit test for FromXmlParser using XmlMapper/XmlFactory to build a real parser from an XML string, favoring the public API over mocks since XMLStreamReader and XmlTokenStream are internal and complex. I need to check whether jackson-dataformat-xml dependencies are actually available on the classpath, since the task implies only certain libs are present. I'm reasoning through whether the Feature enum is empty, which would mean values() returns an empty array and collectDefaults() returns 0 -- something I can verify with a simple test covering nextToken(), getText(), getBinaryValue(), close(), and related methods across different XML inputs. Since Feature has no constants, I can't exercise enable/disable/configure directly, but I can still test getFormatFeatures()/overrideFormatFeatures() using raw int values. I'll design the tests around XmlFactory to build actual parser instances, assuming the full source tree including XmlFactory is available during the Defects4J run. I'm planning several test cases with XmlFactory: one parsing a simple element to verify the token sequence (start object, field name, value, end object, EOF), and another checking how an empty element is handled when checking for leaf content. Next I'm considering an attribute test, planning a self-closing element with just an attribute and no children to test attribute parsing behavior. But I realize I don't have enough certainty about how XmlTokenStream actually handles the root element and attributes without more source context, so I should be cautious about assuming specific token sequences here. Instead, a safer testing strategy is to go through XmlMapper at a higher level, reading XML into Map or JsonNode objects and asserting the resulting structure matches expectations, rather than mocking exact internal tokens. This still exercises the relevant parser branches—simple objects, nested objects, arrays from repeated elements—without needing precise knowledge of internal token constants. For arrays specifically, I'd need to confirm that the parsing context is in an array state, which typically happens when deserializing into a Collection field like List, since XmlMapper auto-wraps repeated elements for list types. I'm sketching concrete tests: checking that collectDefaults returns zero, and parsing a simple two-field XML object into a Map to verify key-value extraction. I also want to cover empty elements (verifying null value handling for self-closing tags) and mixed attribute-plus-text content, which triggers a synthetic empty-named property for the text portion -- I'll use the low-level FromXmlParser to step through the raw token sequence and confirm field names and values appear in the expected order. Without visibility into the internal token stream implementation, I shouldn't guess its exact sequence—better to treat it as a black box and verify behavior observably by deserializing with XmlMapper into POJOs or Maps and checking final values. I'll sketch simple test beans, including ones using attribute and text annotations, though I should confirm those annotations are available in this module before relying on them. For simpler cases, I can fall back to Map-based deserialization. Based on known jackson-dataformat-xml behavior, when a document mixes attributes with text content, attributes get mapped as regular keys and the text content lands under the empty string key, since the default unnamed text property is "". This matches documented source behavior rather than guesswork, so it's legitimate to test. Now I'm sketching out a list of meaningful tests using XmlMapper with Map/List mapping to exercise the relevant branches through public API behavior, starting with checking that feature collection defaults to zero and that format feature overrides work correctly. Then I continue with parsing tests covering simple objects, nested objects into maps, empty elements producing null values, mixed attribute/text handling with the empty-string key, and wrapped array parsing with repeated elements. For the repeated element test, I'm weighing whether to read directly into a Map with a List value using a TypeReference, or to define a small POJO with a List field named to match the repeated element name, since default Jackson naming should align the field to the XML element without needing XML-specific annotations. I'm defining a test where XML with repeated "item" elements maps into a list field on this bean, which exercises Jackson's array-context handling for repeated elements, then adding a follow-up case with a single occurrence to confirm it still produces a single-element list rather than collapsing to a scalar. Next I want to cover empty-element edge cases: deserializing "" into a Map and confirming it yields an empty map, since there's no child element to trigger a FIELD_NAME emission, and then a case where root contains only whitespace text to check how the parser treats whitespace-only content when no start element preceded it. That confirms the empty-map test case. Next I'm sketching further tests: non-whitespace text becomes a field with empty name and the text as value, giving `{"":"hello"}`, and a direct unit test for isExpectedStartArrayToken verifying it flips the token to START_ARRAY and clears the internal next-token state. I should verify XmlFactory.createParser indeed returns a FromXmlParser instance, which it does per the module structure, so casting should be safe. Next I'll test getCurrentName() right after START_OBJECT at the root level — since the root context's current name is likely null, this should trigger an IllegalStateException per the sanity check. Then I want to test getCurrentName() when the token is a FIELD_NAME, which should hit the else branch and return the parsing context's current name directly. I also want to test overrideCurrentName() — setting a custom name while on a FIELD_NAME token and confirming getCurrentName() reflects the override, then checking the same behavior when the current token is START_OBJECT. For binary values, I'm setting up XML with base64-encoded text content like "SGVsbG8=", walking the parser through START_OBJECT and the text-processing branch to reach VALUE_STRING, then calling getBinaryValue() with the default Base64 variant to confirm it correctly decodes to the expected bytes. Next I need tests for error cases: calling getBinaryValue() when currToken isn't VALUE_STRING should throw a JsonParseException, and so should calling it on a VALUE_STRING with malformed base64 characters, since the implementation catches IllegalArgumentException and wraps it. Then I'm planning tests for getText() across different token types—FIELD_NAME should return the current name, VALUE_STRING should return the stored text, and other tokens should fall back to the token's string representation. I also need to check what getText() returns before any token has been read, since the parser doesn't initialize _currToken in its constructor—only on the first call to advance tokens—so a fresh parser's getText() should return null. For getValueAsString() with a default value, I want to cover null currToken, FIELD_NAME, VALUE_STRING, and START_OBJECT cases, though the START_OBJECT behavior depends on XmlTokenStream.convertToString(), which isn't part of the visible source, so I'll need to be cautious about assumptions there. I'm deciding to skip testing the START_OBJECT branch explicitly since its behavior relies on undisclosed internal logic, and instead note that assumption in a comment. For the scalar fallback case, I'll test VALUE_NULL, since JsonToken.VALUE_NULL.isScalarValue() is true and its asString() returns "null", so getValueAsString() should return that default scalar conversion. I'm also planning to test the non-scalar END_OBJECT case, verifying it falls back to a custom default value like "DEF" passed into the method, then sketching out further coverage: always-false hasTextCharacters, always-null getEmbeddedObject, and default-zero/null returns for the various numeric getters (BigInteger, BigDecimal, double, float, int, long, number type, number value). Beyond that, I'm outlining tests for requiring a custom codec, the setCodec/getCodec pair, confirming version() is never null, checking close() is idempotent across repeated calls, and finally probing addVirtualWrapping -- though that one's trickier since it touches a protected field, so I'm thinking through how to verify it indirectly via existing list deserialization coverage or by calling it directly without triggering exceptions. I should also cover low-level FromXmlParser methods not reachable through Map deserialization — things like getBinaryValue, isExpectedStartArrayToken, getCurrentName exceptions, numeric stubs, overrideCurrentName, getValueAsString branches, hasTextCharacters, getEmbeddedObject, requiresCustomCodec, and version/codec accessors — by casting the parser obtained directly from XmlFactory.createParser. Writing imports and test setup... Testing single-element lists, like `1`, should still deserialize into a one-element List because the deserializer checks isExpectedStartArrayToken for the target type, forcing array semantics even when only a single child element is present. I'm wondering if CollectionDeserializer handles a single non-array value by treating it as a one-element list, possibly via ACCEPT_SINGLE_VALUE_AS_ARRAY, though I'm unsure whether XmlMapper enables that by default—this feels like speculation at this point. Since I can't verify that behavior from the given source, I think it's safer to work directly with FromXmlParser's token sequence rather than relying on undocumented Jackson defaults, even though the exact transitions from the underlying token stream aren't fully visible either. Using real collaborating classes like XmlTokenStream, XmlReadContext, and XmlMapper with their actual behavior is fine since that's invoking real code, not guessing—this mirrors how Defects4J blackbox tests typically work for this kind of bug, likely involving array handling or VALUE_NULL logic around empty elements. For the list/array test, I'd rather avoid relying on XmlMapper defaults I'm unsure about, so I'll drop down to the low-level parser and manually call isExpectedStartArrayToken() and nextToken() to simulate what a List deserializer would do, keeping the behavior fully traceable to the actual source logic rather than guessed. Tracing through the nested-array branch, I'm checking whether the mayBeLeaf flag is already set true from when the FIELD_NAME "item" was processed, which determines whether the following XML_TEXT token is treated as a leaf value. If the token at that point is a plain string value rather than START_ARRAY, isExpectedStartArrayToken() would return false, so without single-value-array unwrapping enabled, the deserializer would likely fail rather than coerce the string into a list. This is getting too dependent on jackson-databind internals not visible in the source, so I think it's safer to abandon the List-based test and instead write a direct unit test against isExpectedStartArrayToken() on FromXmlParser itself, manually driving the parser's token state since that behavior is fully specified in the given source -- calling nextToken() to land on START_OBJECT and then checking the result of isExpectedStartArrayToken() directly. I'll verify the true case where START_OBJECT converts to START_ARRAY, then calling it again returns true since the token is now already START_ARRAY, and I'll add a false case by advancing to a FIELD_NAME token and confirming isExpectedStartArrayToken() returns false there. I'll pragmatically split testing: use XmlMapper.readValue into Map for integration-style tests trusting the library's standard XML-to-Map behavior, and use a raw FromXmlParser built via XmlFactory for method-level unit tests like getCurrentName, getBinaryValue, getValueAsString, close, and feature checks. I need a small helper to construct a FromXmlParser from an XML string using XmlFactory.createParser, and I should verify that method signature is supported. Since createParser(String) may not exist on older jackson-core versions, I'll use the safer createParser(Reader) overload with a StringReader, which has been available since the method was renamed from createJsonParser to createParser in 2.1. Adding another test case to confirm field names aren't treated as array starts. Now I'm writing tests for getText() behavior -- checking it's null before any token is consumed, returns the field name when on a FIELD_NAME token, and verifying string value retrieval. I'm also adding tests for getValueAsString(), confirming it returns null (or a provided default) when there's no current token. Writing more test cases... Adding more test cases... Now I'm reviewing potential issues, starting with whether XmlFactory properly supports createParser(Reader) as inherited from JsonFactory's abstract method. I'm verifying the cast from JsonParser to FromXmlParser is valid since XmlFactory's internal method returns FromXmlParser at runtime, then tracing through what happens when nextToken() is first called in the test for checking current name errors - the parser starts with START_OBJECT and creates a child object context. Next I'm tracing through getCurrentName() logic: when current token is START_OBJECT, it looks at the parent context's current name. Since the root context is created fresh with no name ever assigned, this should be null, which aligns with the test's expectation of an IllegalStateException. Then I'm moving to the testGetCurrentNameOnFieldName test case, tracing the second nextToken() call where the XML tokens begin processing the first element. Since this is an object context (not array), the name "a" gets set as current name, mayBeLeaf flips to true, and FIELD_NAME is returned - matching expected behavior. Now I'm checking testIsExpectedStartArrayTokenConvertsStartObject and testEmptyElementProducesValueNull, reasoning through what happens with "" when there's no text content at all between tags, since an empty element wouldn't trigger a CHARACTERS event from the underlying XML parser. This aligns with the source comment documenting the mayBeLeaf-to-VALUE_NULL conversion, which matches the known dataformat-xml#180 behavior. For testWhitespaceOnlyTextSkipsToEndObject with whitespace-only content inside root tags, I'm tracing through how the root element's initial handling differs from nested elements, since root doesn't pass through the same loop that sets mayBeLeaf - meaning the first real token processed for its content would be XML_TEXT directly. With mayBeLeaf still false, this falls into the else branch where the parser checks if we're in an object context with empty text and no field name, collapsing straight to END_OBJECT and restoring the parent context - matching the documented dataformat-xml#177 fix. For the non-empty root text case, I verify it instead sets an empty currentName and returns FIELD_NAME with a pending VALUE_STRING token, which also checks out. Then for the binary value test, I trace through the START_OBJECT, empty FIELD_NAME, and base64-encoded VALUE_STRING sequence to confirm getBinaryValue decodes correctly. Checking the invalid base64 case, I expect the malformed string to trigger an IllegalArgumentException inside the base64 decoding routine, which gets caught and rethrown as a JsonParseException - this is standard jackson-core behavior I can rely on. For the wrong-token-type test, I'm verifying that calling binaryValue on a START_OBJECT token (rather than VALUE_STRING) triggers the error-reporting path that throws JsonParseException by default. I'm also walking through several other tests - checking text length and character extraction against "hi", confirming the XML mapper tests for mixed attributes, empty elements mapping to null, and empty root mapping to an empty map all align with their documented source comments. Now I'm making sure the necessary imports like StringReader and the relevant Jackson classes are included. I'm verifying the imports and method signatures line up correctly - confirming assertArrayEquals and assertSame come from JUnit's Assert class, checking that getValueAsString can be called directly, and reviewing how overrideFormatFeatures initializes the format features field. Since XmlFactory's default format feature flags likely start at 0 given no enabled features by default, I'm reasoning through whether the test's assertion of zero format features will hold reliably across different construction paths. Now checking the "testGetValueAsStringDefaultForNonScalarEndObject" test: with "", after START_OBJECT the next token call should collapse directly to END_OBJECT since there's no text content at all, similar to how an empty string returns true for the emptiness check. Tracing through the alternative path too: if the parser goes straight from START_ELEMENT to END_ELEMENT without a text event, the end result is still END_OBJECT via the default case. Either way the behavior converges, so the test holds regardless of which internal branch fires. Checking getValueAsString("DEF") on END_OBJECT - since END_OBJECT isn't a scalar value, it falls through to return the default. That matches expectations. Similarly testGetValueAsStringNullToken checks out fine, and since our test class shares the package with FromXmlParser, accessing package-private members like DEFAULT_UNNAMED_TEXT_PROPERTY works without issue. I'm also planning a test for array handling using isExpectedStartArrayToken, simulating XML like repeated item elements under a root to walk through the token sequence manually. Since the token returned would just be VALUE_STRING without an array wrapper, this edge case is too uncertain to pin down reliably, so I'll skip it per my rule of not guessing. I already have solid coverage, so I'll just add a couple more boundary tests, like checking _isEmpty with a single non-space character. The whitespace-only and "hello" test cases already cover the _isEmpty branches well, and the empty root element test confirms the zero-length string case returns true immediately. I just need to double-check that the invalid base64 test string with exclamation marks is valid as plain XML text content without needing escaping. Since '!' isn't a valid base64 character, Jackson's Base64Variant.decode should throw IllegalArgumentException on it rather than silently skip it, which matches expected test behavior. I also want to confirm the getBinaryValue method uses _reportError to produce a proper JsonParseException consistent with ParserMinimalBase's error-handling conventions. The test suite looks complete now, so I'll finalize the response with the full code and an explanatory summary table in Thai mapping each test method to the branch it covers, making sure all test methods declare the proper IOException throws clause.
